plan.title: Advanced Upper/Lower Strength Builder
plan.description: A heavy 4-day routine focused on low-rep, high-weight compound movements to maximize power and raw strength.

workouts.title: Upper Day 1: Heavy Horizontal
workouts.description: Focuses on maximizing raw strength in horizontal pushing and pulling patterns.

workouts.title: Lower Day 1: Heavy Squat Focus
workouts.description: Focuses on maximizing raw strength in the squat pattern and heavy hinging.

workouts.title: Upper Day 2: Heavy Vertical
workouts.description: Focuses on maximizing raw strength in vertical pushing and pulling patterns.

workouts.title: Lower Day 2: Heavy Hinge Focus
workouts.description: Focuses on maximizing raw pulling strength from the floor and unilateral leg power.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: The standard compound movement for developing chest mass and upper body pushing power.
exercises.instruction: 1. Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar. 2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulders. 3. Lower the bar to mid-chest. 4. Press back up until arms are locked.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.description: A heavy compound horizontal pulling exercise that builds mass and strength in the upper and middle back.
exercises.instruction: 1. Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. 2. Grab the barbell and pull it towards your lower ribcage. 3. Lower the weight under control.

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.description: A vertical press focusing on raw strength in the anterior and lateral deltoids.
exercises.instruction: 1. Stand with a barbell resting on your front shoulders. 2. Press the weight upward until arms are locked out straight. 3. Lower slowly back to the start.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-Up
exercises.description: An advanced variation of the pull-up designed to aggressively overload the back and lats for strength and width.
exercises.instruction: 1. Attach a weight belt. 2. Grip the pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width. 3. Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar. 4. Lower down with control.

exercises.name: Barbell Squat
exercises.description: The king of lower body exercises for quads and glutes, essential for raw leg strength.
exercises.instruction: 1. Place bar on upper back. 2. Squat down until thighs are parallel to floor. 3. Drive heavily through heels to stand up.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A heavy hinge movement focusing on hamstrings and glutes for posterior chain strength.
exercises.instruction: 1. Hold barbell at hip height. 2. Push hips back while lowering bar down legs. 3. Feel stretch in hamstrings and drive hips forward to return to start.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.description: Machine-based movement to overload the legs with high weight safely.
exercises.instruction: 1. Sit in machine with feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Lower platform toward chest. 3. Press back up heavily without locking knees.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.instruction: 1. Stand on a raised surface with a barbell or in a calf raise machine. 2. Push through the balls of your feet to raise your body. 3. Lower slowly.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.description: A horizontal pull focusing on the rhomboids and middle back.
exercises.instruction: 1. Sit with feet on pads, knees slightly bent. 2. Pull handle toward abdomen. 3. Squeeze shoulder blades together. 4. Extend arms back.

exercises.name: Conventional Deadlift
exercises.description: The ultimate full-body raw strength builder, primarily taxing the posterior chain and core.
exercises.instruction: 1. Stand with mid-foot under the barbell. 2. Bend over and grab the bar. 3. Bend knees until shins touch the bar. 4. Lift chest, straighten lower back, and stand up with the weight.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.description: A challenging unilateral leg exercise focusing heavily on the quads and glutes, allowing for overload safely.
exercises.instruction: 1. Stand a few feet in front of a bench holding heavy dumbbells. 2. Place one foot behind you on the bench. 3. Lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the ground. 4. Drive back up.
